ShortDescription.Value: Fix Not Enough Customers icons by balancing commercial shop production and shopping demand.

Publish.LongDescription:
# 🛒 ## "Not Enough Customers" icons everywhere?
Got 100's of NEC icons? Adding more citizens doesn't always help!
#### Struggling shops don't get enough priority * NEC icons appear when a shop goes over 90% unused Service (different from stock). * One vanilla shopping score puts **50%–100% full shops in the same bucket**. A shop at 95% full gets no more help from that score than one at 60%. * So citizens can keep choosing healthier stores while others still sit ignored above 90% and explode with NEC icons.
### Why this happens
* Shop workers get paid to produce Service. Service is not stock, it's different from the goods delivered to it (food, paper...). * Vanilla starts slowing production a little at 80% unused Service. By 90% critical threshold, it's still producing too much. It doesn't clamp to 0 until the shop hits 100% full Service, way too late. * Cims at work/school are not allowed to shop, so peak periods have less eligible shoppers as only elderly and or those not in school/work are available.
**Shops end up making Service faster than shoppers can use it.** Adding more citizens doesn't always fix this, when struggling shops aren't getting enough priority. Smarter cims help balance shopping demand.
### What this mod does
* Just install the mod and play! No Options menu or settings to configure. * **Starts helping at ~82% full Service**, before the critical 90% threshold causes an alert icon. Many rates were heavily tested to optimize for good, realistic rate buckets/balance. * **Slows production harder** when shops are too full. Once healthy again (below 82% shop), it goes back to vanilla to handle things normally. * **Helps balance shopping demand** using existing households, not fake shoppers. * **Separately helps Leisure** businesses (Meals, Entertainment, Recreation). * **Best-effort help for hotels**, using existing tourists as Hotels are based on total rooms rented. No fake tourists added. * Example, I had 700 tourist and 8 hotels with 9000 rooms, the mod reduced my hotel NEC from 8 to 4 by adaptive priorities. After that I had to delete a couple or switch to static hotels.
### Some test results
* **130k city:** 165 NEC → 4 after ~30 minutes. * **90k city (Sunny Isle):** 335 NEC → 30 after 10 minutes, 9 after 20 minutes.
### What to expect
* **Give heavily affected cities 15–20 minutes** to rebalance; many changes happen within 5 minutes. * If you have a small number 15-20 left after ~30 minutes, this is the time to prune a few excess shops. They don't have to be the exact ones showing NEC. * It won't fix every case of legit excess commercial zoning or poor access to shops. * Safe to remove. Vanilla balancing takes over again. No Harmony patch or invasive system replacement methods used.
